texts: bad: with a bare "When", the translator took this as a one-off report and asserted both halves outright — the moon IS full and a convening DID happen — so nothing conditional survives in the knowledge base. Make the recurrence explicit: "Whenever the moon is full, the Council convenes at the Watch." — your next sentence, worded that way, parsed as a proper per-occasion rule.
good. parses as a fireable per-occasion rule that ties each meeting to the full moon triggering it, and correctly asserts neither a full moon nor a meeting on its own.
